pages.main_text_excerpt:
CeMAT 2026: Beyond the hardware, and what really drives automation performance
At CeMAT Australia 2026, Element Logic hosted a workshop focused on questions many warehouse leaders are facing such as what actually determines the success of an automation project, and how do you ask the right questions early to avoid costly surprises later?
While robots, conveyors and storage systems often take center stage, they are rarely what makes or breaks performance. Instead, the real drivers sit behind the scenes in software, simulation, data and compliance.
Bringing together expertise from both inside and outside Element Logic, the session explored how these elements work together to de-risk projects, improve decision-making, and create long-term operational value.
From systems to solutions
As Group Chief Product Officer Christian Rognes highlighted, the conversation around automation is shifting. It is no longer about standalone technologies, but about how to connect them into a cohesive system. 
 
Element Logic’s approach reflects this shift. By combining robotics with a growing software portfolio including analytics platforms like eLogiq, and integrating with existing warehouse and business systems, the company helps customers move from fragmented solutions to fully connected, end-to-end automation environments.
			
The data will be the differentiator going forward. Regardless of how you look at it, if you cannot extract the data from your systems and workflows, you cannot use it for anything else
Christian Rognes, Group Chief Product Officer at Element Logic
This integration is what enables real performance gains. Data from across the operation can be collected, analyzed and used to optimize workflows, predict maintenance needs and reduce downtime turning automation from a one-time investment into a continuously improving system.
Rognes also emphasized the importance of building flexibility into automation strategies from the outset: “If you have an accurate and rich data model, you can create a digital twin of your warehouse and you can simulate every change – you can visualize it and you can test it. You de-risk everything you do. It also gives you a platform to innovate and test new technologies before you actually do it.”
Reducing risk before the first robot is installed
A second key theme in the session was the role of simulation and digital modelling, presented by Samir Rafiq, Head of Automation at Element Logic ANZ.
			
There are many considerations we have to make at the start, because if you don’t, it’s not as simple as throwing more robots at it
Samir Rafiq, Head of Automation at Element Logic ANZ
Modern warehouse design increasingly relies on digital twins (virtual representations of warehouse systems that make it possible to test layouts), processes and scenarios before physical installation begins. These models allow teams to validate throughput assumptions, identify bottlenecks and refine designs early in the process.
Simulation is not only about design. It also supports ongoing optimization, enabling teams to experiment with new strategies, forecast demand and adapt operations without disrupting live systems.
This goes to show that high-quality data and realistic forecasting are critical. Without them, even well-designed systems risk underperforming. With them, companies can make more informed investment decisions and reduce costly rework later.
As Rafiq put it: “Throughput is the promise that you sign up for.”
Designing for safety and compliance from day one
Fire safety and compliance was addressed by Colin Yeo, Director of Warehouse Focus, who emphasized the importance of embedding fire protection into the design process from the very beginning. Warehouse environments are classified as “ultrafast” in terms of fire growth, underscoring the need for early detection and rapid response.
			
When you first start an automation project, particularly in the planning and design phase, it’s important to understand the fire requirements
Colin Yeo, Director of Warehouse Focus
He highlighted how fire behavior differs depending on storage configuration, and how automated systems require carefully designed detection and sprinkler strategies to ensure fires can be contained and extinguished effectively.
Just as important is the compliance process itself, which involves coordination between fire engineers, authorities, insurers and other stakeholders, and typically takes several months to complete.
Designing with compliance in mind
The session also addressed a topic that is often misunderstood: fire safety and compliance in automated warehouses.
Drawing on extensive testing and industry guidelines, the discussion showed how fire protection is not an afterthought, but an integrated part of system design. For example, long-term testing has demonstrated how different protection methods, including sprinkler systems, can effectively control and extinguish fires in automated storage systems.

Element Logic and Ranpak Announce Strategic Global Partnership to Strengthen Warehouse Automation Offering
The partnership combines warehouse automation expertise and packaging automation technology to help customers improve efficiency, reduce waste, and create more integrated fulfilment operations.
Oslo, Norway, 29 September 2026 – Element Logic has entered into a strategic global partnership with Ranpak, a leading provider of sustainable packaging automation solutions. The collaboration will integrate Ranpak’s end-of-line packaging automation technology into Element Logic’s warehouse automation portfolio, enabling customers to benefit from more efficient, scalable, and sustainable fulfilment solutions.
As customer expectations continue to rise and new sustainability regulations such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) are introduced, businesses are looking for smarter ways to optimize warehouse operations from picking and packing through to shipping. Through this partnership, Element Logic customers will gain access to packaging automation technologies that can help reduce packaging material usage, lower shipped volume, and improve overall packing efficiency.
Shared ambition
The partnership builds on an existing relationship between the two companies and reflects a shared ambition to create more connected warehouse operations. By combining Element Logic’s expertise in warehouse automation, software, and systems integration with Ranpak’s capabilities in rightsizing, box forming, closing, computer vision, and paper-based product protection, customers can benefit from a more streamlined outbound logistics flow.
Rather than treating packaging as a separate process, the integrated approach enables businesses to design picking, packing, and shipping as part of one cohesive operation. Ranpak’s automation technology replaces manual box-building with systems that automatically select, erect, and right-size packaging for each order, helping increase throughput, consistency, and transportation efficiency while reducing packaging waste.
			
At Element Logic, we continuously expand our solution portfolio to help customers optimize warehouse performance from inbound processes to final shipment. Partnering with Ranpak strengthens our packaging offering and enables us to deliver even greater value through integrated, scalable and sustainable solutions
Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic
“We are proud to build this partnership with Element Logic, providing a trusted offering that covers end-of-line packaging processes while working synergistically with other core solutions in their implementations. With Ranpak playing a role in these integrations, Element Logic is offering their customers the pinnacle of flexibility and efficiency as they design and integrate intralogistics flows,” says Omar Asali, CEO of Ranpak.
The partnership supports Element Logic’s ambition to deliver end-to-end warehouse solutions across the entire value chain, from inbound logistics and storage to order fulfilment, packaging, and final shipment. By broadening its solution portfolio, Element Logic continues to help customers improve operational performance while meeting evolving sustainability and business requirements.

pages.title: From vision to global leadership - 40 years of passion and innovation - Element Logic
pages.main_text_excerpt:
From vision to global leadership – 40 years of passion and innovation
As we mark Element Logic’s 40th anniversary, it’s the perfect opportunity to celebrate a remarkable journey that began in 1985. From humble beginnings in Norway, two visionary brothers – Kjell and Dag-Adler Blakseth – shared a dream of optimizing warehouse performance and making businesses more efficient. This shared vision laid the foundation for the global success story we see today.
The Early Years: A Modest Start with Big Ambitions
Starting out as a small Norwegian business, the Blakseth brothers began by enhancing warehouse workflows with innovative yet simple solutions, like writing software based on a stopwatch and manually counting warehouse worker steps. Their approach was bold yet grounded in practical efficiency – a characteristic that remains at the core of Element Logic.
A Breakthrough Moment: The AutoStore Collaboration
In 2003, Element Logic entered a new chapter when Kjell Blakseth crossed paths with Ingvar Hognaland, the inventor of AutoStore, at a tradeshow. Dag-Adler Blakseth, known for his strategic insight and entrepreneurial drive, played a pivotal role in supporting the decision to embrace AutoStore’s “crazy robot idea.” Within six months, the brothers led the creation of the world’s first AutoStore system, establishing a partnership that would revolutionize the industry and define Element Logic’s trajectory.
Expansion and Global Reach
Under Dag-Adler and Kjell’s leadership, Element Logic rapidly grew, first becoming a market leader in the Nordics and then expanding across Europe. In 2015, the company completed its first AutoStore project outside the region, and by 2020, it held full European distribution rights. The vision continued to guide the company during this period of remarkable growth, including the acquisitions that opened doors to new markets in the Americas and most recently Asia-Pacific’s.
“When we started Element Logic 40 years ago, our vision was simple: to optimize warehouse performance through innovation and efficiency. Today, I’m proud to see how our brave ideas, passionate people, and reliable solutions have shaped a global success story – and we’re just getting started”, says Dag-Adler Blakseth, Co-Founder of Element Logic, and Chairman of the Board.
			
…I’m proud to see how our brave ideas, passionate people, and reliable solutions have shaped a global success story – and we’re just getting started
Dag-Adler Blakseth, Co-Founder of Element Logic, and Chairman of the Board
Today: A Global Leader with a People-First Approach
By 2025, Element Logic has become one of the largest system integrators globally, serving clients across continents. Despite our technological success, the Blakseth brothers’ legacy of valuing people above all else remains central to our identity. The focus on fostering an open, respectful, and humble workplace culture has become a cornerstone of who we are as a company.
Looking Ahead: Shaping the Future of Warehousing
As we celebrate 40 years of excellence, we also set our sights firmly on the future. Element Logic is ready to continue leading the way in warehouse automation by offering a fully interconnected ecosystem of data-driven software solutions, cutting-edge technology, AI-powered solutions, and the innovative spirit that has defined us since 1985.
By offering our solutions that optimize space, reduce waste, and minimize emissions, we empower our clients to achieve a smaller carbon footprint while enhancing operational efficiency. Committed to driving a greener future, we continue to integrate innovative technologies and sustainable practices, ensuring that sustainability remains important in our mission to revolutionize warehousing worldwide.
“As we mark 40 years of achievements, we eagerly anticipate a future full of opportunities. Our focus remains on driving growth by scaling our operations, embracing digital transformation, and maintaining leadership in warehouse automation. It’s a journey that demands bravery, passion, and reliability – values that lie at the heart of who we are”, says Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic.
			
…It’s a journey that demands bravery, passion, and reliability – values that lie at the heart of who we are
Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic
With a growing global presence and a passionate team committed to solving tomorrow’s challenges, we aim to revolutionize warehousing on an even larger scale. Together, we will continue to innovate, expand, and adapt – ensuring that Element Logic remains at the forefront of the industry for decades to come.
Looking at our remarkable 40-year journey, we thank our employees, partners, and customers for your trust and collaboration. Together, we have optimized warehousing for decades, and together, we will revolutionize it for years to come.
We are grateful for 40 years of brave innovation, passionate service, and reliable partnerships, and look forward to many more to come.

pages.title: How today's students help explore tomorrow's warehouse - Element Logic
pages.main_text_excerpt:
How today’s students help explore tomorrow’s warehouse
Every summer, Element Logic brings talented engineering and technology students into its R&D organization to work on real-world challenges.
Many come from leading universities in Germany, US and Norway such as NTNU and UIUC, where they study fields including computer science, artificial intelligence, cybernetics, robotics and software engineering. The internship program has become a sought-after opportunity for students eager to apply their skills to real business challenges.
For the students, it is an opportunity to apply their knowledge to real-world problems. For Element Logic, it is a chance to explore emerging technologies, challenge assumptions, and gain fresh perspectives on what the future of warehousing might look like.
This year, three internship projects have been running across Norway and Germany, each focused on a different aspect of warehouse automation. Together, they offer a glimpse into technologies that could influence how warehouses operate in the years ahead.
Investing in talent and the future
The internship program is designed around real business challenges rather than theoretical assignments. Students work closely with experienced engineers and developers, contributing to projects that align with Element Logic’s long-term innovation priorities.
			
Many companies focus on technologies that are already mature. We also need to understand the technologies that are emerging and determine where they may create value in the future. Internship projects give us an opportunity to build knowledge, test ideas, and explore new possibilities.
Christian Rognes, Chief Product Officer at Element Logic
The projects also reflect the company’s broader ambition to combine software, data, robotics, and automation into intelligent end-to-end warehouse solutions.
Project 1: Can humanoid robots create value in warehouses?
One of the teams has spent the summer at our headquarters in Kløfta exploring an increasingly visible technology trend: humanoid robots.
While humanoids often attract attention through videos on social media, the objective of the project has been far more practical. The team has investigated where humanoid robots could realistically create value in warehouse environments and what would be required before such technology makes sense in real-world operations.
Potential use cases include goods receiving, handling irregular items, and tasks that vary from day to day. The work combines warehouse process understanding, software development, simulation, artificial intelligence, and robotics to evaluate both technical feasibility and business value.
“Technology should be applied where it creates real value. Our ambition is a warehouse where people, software, and automation work seamlessly together. That allows employees to spend less time on repetitive or physically demanding tasks and more time applying their experience, judgment, and operational knowledge,” says Rognes.
Project 2: Turning experience into knowledge with Project BEACON
The second team has focused on a different challenge: how to make years of organizational knowledge easier to find and use.
Project BEACON (Business Enrichment, Analytics & Customer Opportunity Navigator) explores how artificial intelligence can help employees retrieve relevant knowledge from previous projects, documents, and data sources within seconds.

Element Logic and Ranpak Announce Strategic Global Partnership to Strengthen Warehouse Automation Offering
The partnership combines warehouse automation expertise and packaging automation technology to help customers improve efficiency, reduce waste, and create more integrated fulfilment operations.
Oslo, Norway, 29 September 2026 – Element Logic has entered into a strategic global partnership with Ranpak, a leading provider of sustainable packaging automation solutions. The collaboration will integrate Ranpak’s end-of-line packaging automation technology into Element Logic’s warehouse automation portfolio, enabling customers to benefit from more efficient, scalable, and sustainable fulfilment solutions.
As customer expectations continue to rise and new sustainability regulations such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) are introduced, businesses are looking for smarter ways to optimize warehouse operations from picking and packing through to shipping. Through this partnership, Element Logic customers will gain access to packaging automation technologies that can help reduce packaging material usage, lower shipped volume, and improve overall packing efficiency.
Shared ambition
The partnership builds on an existing relationship between the two companies and reflects a shared ambition to create more connected warehouse operations. By combining Element Logic’s expertise in warehouse automation, software, and systems integration with Ranpak’s capabilities in rightsizing, box forming, closing, computer vision, and paper-based product protection, customers can benefit from a more streamlined outbound logistics flow.
Rather than treating packaging as a separate process, the integrated approach enables businesses to design picking, packing, and shipping as part of one cohesive operation. Ranpak’s automation technology replaces manual box-building with systems that automatically select, erect, and right-size packaging for each order, helping increase throughput, consistency, and transportation efficiency while reducing packaging waste.
			
At Element Logic, we continuously expand our solution portfolio to help customers optimize warehouse performance from inbound processes to final shipment. Partnering with Ranpak strengthens our packaging offering and enables us to deliver even greater value through integrated, scalable and sustainable solutions
Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic
“We are proud to build this partnership with Element Logic, providing a trusted offering that covers end-of-line packaging processes while working synergistically with other core solutions in their implementations. With Ranpak playing a role in these integrations, Element Logic is offering their customers the pinnacle of flexibility and efficiency as they design and integrate intralogistics flows,” says Omar Asali, CEO of Ranpak.
The partnership supports Element Logic’s ambition to deliver end-to-end warehouse solutions across the entire value chain, from inbound logistics and storage to order fulfilment, packaging, and final shipment. By broadening its solution portfolio, Element Logic continues to help customers improve operational performance while meeting evolving sustainability and business requirements.

pages.title: From vision to global leadership - 40 years of passion and innovation - Element Logic
pages.main_text_excerpt:
From vision to global leadership – 40 years of passion and innovation
As we mark Element Logic’s 40th anniversary, it’s the perfect opportunity to celebrate a remarkable journey that began in 1985. From humble beginnings in Norway, two visionary brothers – Kjell and Dag-Adler Blakseth – shared a dream of optimizing warehouse performance and making businesses more efficient. This shared vision laid the foundation for the global success story we see today.
The Early Years: A Modest Start with Big Ambitions
Starting out as a small Norwegian business, the Blakseth brothers began by enhancing warehouse workflows with innovative yet simple solutions, like writing software based on a stopwatch and manually counting warehouse worker steps. Their approach was bold yet grounded in practical efficiency – a characteristic that remains at the core of Element Logic.
A Breakthrough Moment: The AutoStore Collaboration
In 2003, Element Logic entered a new chapter when Kjell Blakseth crossed paths with Ingvar Hognaland, the inventor of AutoStore, at a tradeshow. Dag-Adler Blakseth, known for his strategic insight and entrepreneurial drive, played a pivotal role in supporting the decision to embrace AutoStore’s “crazy robot idea.” Within six months, the brothers led the creation of the world’s first AutoStore system, establishing a partnership that would revolutionize the industry and define Element Logic’s trajectory.
Expansion and Global Reach
Under Dag-Adler and Kjell’s leadership, Element Logic rapidly grew, first becoming a market leader in the Nordics and then expanding across Europe. In 2015, the company completed its first AutoStore project outside the region, and by 2020, it held full European distribution rights. The vision continued to guide the company during this period of remarkable growth, including the acquisitions that opened doors to new markets in the Americas and most recently Asia-Pacific’s.
“When we started Element Logic 40 years ago, our vision was simple: to optimize warehouse performance through innovation and efficiency. Today, I’m proud to see how our brave ideas, passionate people, and reliable solutions have shaped a global success story – and we’re just getting started”, says Dag-Adler Blakseth, Co-Founder of Element Logic, and Chairman of the Board.
			
…I’m proud to see how our brave ideas, passionate people, and reliable solutions have shaped a global success story – and we’re just getting started
Dag-Adler Blakseth, Co-Founder of Element Logic, and Chairman of the Board
Today: A Global Leader with a People-First Approach
By 2025, Element Logic has become one of the largest system integrators globally, serving clients across continents. Despite our technological success, the Blakseth brothers’ legacy of valuing people above all else remains central to our identity. The focus on fostering an open, respectful, and humble workplace culture has become a cornerstone of who we are as a company.
Looking Ahead: Shaping the Future of Warehousing
As we celebrate 40 years of excellence, we also set our sights firmly on the future. Element Logic is ready to continue leading the way in warehouse automation by offering a fully interconnected ecosystem of data-driven software solutions, cutting-edge technology, AI-powered solutions, and the innovative spirit that has defined us since 1985.
By offering our solutions that optimize space, reduce waste, and minimize emissions, we empower our clients to achieve a smaller carbon footprint while enhancing operational efficiency. Committed to driving a greener future, we continue to integrate innovative technologies and sustainable practices, ensuring that sustainability remains important in our mission to revolutionize warehousing worldwide.
“As we mark 40 years of achievements, we eagerly anticipate a future full of opportunities. Our focus remains on driving growth by scaling our operations, embracing digital transformation, and maintaining leadership in warehouse automation. It’s a journey that demands bravery, passion, and reliability – values that lie at the heart of who we are”, says Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic.
			
…It’s a journey that demands bravery, passion, and reliability – values that lie at the heart of who we are
Ankush Malhotra, Group CEO of Element Logic
With a growing global presence and a passionate team committed to solving tomorrow’s challenges, we aim to revolutionize warehousing on an even larger scale. Together, we will continue to innovate, expand, and adapt – ensuring that Element Logic remains at the forefront of the industry for decades to come.
Looking at our remarkable 40-year journey, we thank our employees, partners, and customers for your trust and collaboration. Together, we have optimized warehousing for decades, and together, we will revolutionize it for years to come.
We are grateful for 40 years of brave innovation, passionate service, and reliable partnerships, and look forward to many more to come.

How today’s students help explore tomorrow’s warehouse
Every summer, Element Logic brings talented engineering and technology students into its R&D organization to work on real-world challenges.
Many come from leading universities in Germany, US and Norway such as NTNU and UIUC, where they study fields including computer science, artificial intelligence, cybernetics, robotics and software engineering. The internship program has become a sought-after opportunity for students eager to apply their skills to real business challenges.
For the students, it is an opportunity to apply their knowledge to real-world problems. For Element Logic, it is a chance to explore emerging technologies, challenge assumptions, and gain fresh perspectives on what the future of warehousing might look like.
This year, three internship projects have been running across Norway and Germany, each focused on a different aspect of warehouse automation. Together, they offer a glimpse into technologies that could influence how warehouses operate in the years ahead.
Investing in talent and the future
The internship program is designed around real business challenges rather than theoretical assignments. Students work closely with experienced engineers and developers, contributing to projects that align with Element Logic’s long-term innovation priorities.
			
Many companies focus on technologies that are already mature. We also need to understand the technologies that are emerging and determine where they may create value in the future. Internship projects give us an opportunity to build knowledge, test ideas, and explore new possibilities.
Christian Rognes, Chief Product Officer at Element Logic
The projects also reflect the company’s broader ambition to combine software, data, robotics, and automation into intelligent end-to-end warehouse solutions.
Project 1: Can humanoid robots create value in warehouses?
One of the teams has spent the summer at our headquarters in Kløfta exploring an increasingly visible technology trend: humanoid robots.
While humanoids often attract attention through videos on social media, the objective of the project has been far more practical. The team has investigated where humanoid robots could realistically create value in warehouse environments and what would be required before such technology makes sense in real-world operations.
Potential use cases include goods receiving, handling irregular items, and tasks that vary from day to day. The work combines warehouse process understanding, software development, simulation, artificial intelligence, and robotics to evaluate both technical feasibility and business value.
“Technology should be applied where it creates real value. Our ambition is a warehouse where people, software, and automation work seamlessly together. That allows employees to spend less time on repetitive or physically demanding tasks and more time applying their experience, judgment, and operational knowledge,” says Rognes.
Project 2: Turning experience into knowledge with Project BEACON
The second team has focused on a different challenge: how to make years of organizational knowledge easier to find and use.
Project BEACON (Business Enrichment, Analytics & Customer Opportunity Navigator) explores how artificial intelligence can help employees retrieve relevant knowledge from previous projects, documents, and data sources within seconds.
In many organizations, valuable experience already exists, but it is often scattered across systems, reports, emails, and teams. BEACON investigates how AI can make that knowledge searchable, actionable, and available exactly when it is needed.
			
Rather than building just another chatbot, we are looking at how AI can help people access relevant and trustworthy information. If we can make lessons learned from previous projects easier to find and apply, we can make better and faster decisions in future customer projects.
Nils Stanelle, Senior Software Engineer at Element Logic
The project works with technologies such as semantic search, language models, and knowledge structures to explore how AI can transform existing experience into a practical asset for the organization.

The third internship project marks the program’s first international R&D internship initiative and is being conducted in Germany.

Instead of relying solely on predefined rules, future systems may be able to react dynamically to what is actually happening in the warehouse at any given moment.
The goal is to better understand how operational data can support more intelligent software, more responsive warehouse operations, and improved decision-making.

CeMAT 2026: Beyond the hardware, and what really drives automation performance
At CeMAT Australia 2026, Element Logic hosted a workshop focused on questions many warehouse leaders are facing such as what actually determines the success of an automation project, and how do you ask the right questions early to avoid costly surprises later?
While robots, conveyors and storage systems often take center stage, they are rarely what makes or breaks performance. Instead, the real drivers sit behind the scenes in software, simulation, data and compliance.
Bringing together expertise from both inside and outside Element Logic, the session explored how these elements work together to de-risk projects, improve decision-making, and create long-term operational value.
From systems to solutions

Element Logic’s approach reflects this shift. By combining robotics with a growing software portfolio including analytics platforms like eLogiq, and integrating with existing warehouse and business systems, the company helps customers move from fragmented solutions to fully connected, end-to-end automation environments.
			
The data will be the differentiator going forward. Regardless of how you look at it, if you cannot extract the data from your systems and workflows, you cannot use it for anything else

This integration is what enables real performance gains. Data from across the operation can be collected, analyzed and used to optimize workflows, predict maintenance needs and reduce downtime turning automation from a one-time investment into a continuously improving system.
Rognes also emphasized the importance of building flexibility into automation strategies from the outset: “If you have an accurate and rich data model, you can create a digital twin of your warehouse and you can simulate every change – you can visualize it and you can test it. You de-risk everything you do. It also gives you a platform to innovate and test new technologies before you actually do it.”
